tips.title: Include All 10 Required Elements in a Public Notice
tips.summary: Prepare drinking-water public notices that clearly explain the violation and include all 10 elements identified in the EPA Public Notification Rule reference.
steps: Explain the violation clearly and in plain language.
Include the 10 elements: violation, contaminant, timing, health effects, vulnerable populations, alternate water use, consumer actions, system response, compliance timeline, and contact information.
Check the notice against the EPA Public Notification Rule reference before distribution.
warnings: This tip summarizes notice content; it is not a substitute for checking the current rule and jurisdiction-specific requirements.
tips.evidence_excerpt: All public notices must include a clear and readily understandable explanation of each violation containing the following 10 elements from EPA’s Public Notification Rule (PNR) Quick Reference Guide.

tips.summary: Plastic sheeting can be an important emergency-shelter component, often combined with rigid materials; it needs suitable support and has limitations in severe weather.

warnings: Plastic sheeting alone does not provide strong resistance to high winds or heavy rain.

steps: For tropical or warm climates, use 3.5 m² per person as the cited minimum covered living-space figure.

tips.title: Use Adequate Heating Stoves in Cold Environments
tips.summary: UNHCR gives 5–7 kW as an indicative stove output for heating 40–70 m² in many cold areas, depending on conditions; it is not a universal sizing rule.
steps: Treat 5–7 kW for 40–70 m² only as an indicative reference from the cited UNHCR guidance.
Assess outside temperature, building construction, insulation, orientation, and actual stove performance before selecting heating equipment.
Follow appropriate installation, ventilation, and fire-safety requirements.
warnings: Heating needs vary with conditions; the UNHCR entry is marked outdated and under revision. Poorly installed fuel-burning stoves can cause fire and carbon-monoxide hazards.
